# Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

```{r}
#| label: p4-conc-setup
#| include: false
c_pool_B1 <- cf(p4_arm_grid_pooled, "B1", "mod")
c_pool_B2 <- cf(p4_arm_grid_pooled, "B2", "mod")
```

Blended with the starting price on `r comma(n_common)` held-out races,
the model contributes `r fmt_b(c_pool_B1$estimate)` and
`r fmt_b(c_pool_B2$estimate)`.

That raises the bar for paper 5. Paper 3 pointed at a learned
representation of a horse's run history in place of hand-built summaries
of it. If the settled market already prices what these features carry,
compressing the same histories more efficiently produces a model that is
already priced, however good the compression. The representation has to
extract something the summaries discard *and* that the market has not
itself inferred.

Anyone else using Smartform should note @sec-appx-provenance: the two
forecast-price columns disagree on a third of rows, and the
documentation gives no reason why.
